cut.note: the unscented Kalman filter's two reusable pieces, read as the mechanism the library is cited for: a deterministic set of 2n+1 sigma points placed by the matrix square root of the covariance and scaled by (alpha, beta, kappa), and an unscented transform that pushes those points through a nonlinear function and recovers a mean and covariance by weighted sums, with hooks so that quantities living on a manifold (angles) can supply their own mean and residual operators

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_name: MerweScaledSigmaPoints.sigma_points (124-178): lambda_ = alpha^2 (n + kappa) - n; U = cholesky((lambda_ + n) P); point 0 = x, points i = x +/- U_i; _compute_weights (180-195): Wm and Wc with Wc[0] adding (1 - alpha^2 + beta)
organs.mechanism: for an n-dimensional Gaussian (x, P) the filter forms 2n+1 points: the mean, and the mean plus and minus each column of the scaled matrix square root sqrt((lambda_ + n) P) (Cholesky by default); the spread is set by alpha (small = tight around the mean), the extra weight on the zeroth point's covariance by beta (2 is optimal for a Gaussian), and kappa is a secondary scaling; the mean weights Wm and covariance weights Wc differ only in the zeroth entry
assumptions: a Gaussian is captured to second order by these deterministic points, so a nonlinear map's output mean and covariance are recovered without a Jacobian (the unscented transform's premise, Julier & Uhlmann 1997)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a derivative-free nonlinear filter: no Jacobian, better than the EKF on strong nonlinearities
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a non-positive-definite P makes the Cholesky fail (a known UKF fragility; the sqrt_method hook exists to swap in a more robust root)
organs.human_prior: Julier & Uhlmann 1997; Wan & van der Merwe 2000 (the scaled form)

organs.human_name: unscented_transform (22-110): x = Wm . sigmas (or mean_fn); P = sum Wc (y - x)(y - x)^T + noise_cov, with residual_fn for the (y - x) so angular states subtract mod 2pi
organs.mechanism: the sigma points are passed through the process or measurement function outside the transform; the transform then computes the output mean as the Wm-weighted sum of the transformed points (or a caller-supplied circular mean for angles), and the output covariance as the Wc-weighted sum of outer products of the residuals plus an additive noise covariance; a residual function lets states that are not closed under subtraction (angles, quaternions) define their own difference so the covariance is correct on the manifold
organs.input: transformed sigma points, the weights, an optional noise covariance
assumptions: the weighted sums reproduce the true transformed moments to second order; manifold states need custom mean/residual to avoid wraparound errors
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the same transform serves the predict and the update of the UKF; the manifold hooks are why FilterPy is used for attitude and heading filters

pressures.source_evidence: sigma_points.py; unscented_transform.py; the record's example systems
pressures.condition: an organism tracks a state through nonlinear process and measurement functions; linearisation (the EKF) is inaccurate; some components are angles that wrap; the score is estimate error and consistency against a linear-Gaussian ground truth where one exists
pressures.resource_or_constraint: 2n+1 function evaluations per step; a covariance square root
pressures.failure_condition: divergence on strong nonlinearity (EKF's failure), or a covariance corrupted by treating angular residuals as linear
pressures.world_punishes: a Jacobian-based filter on a non-smooth map; naive subtraction of angles
pressures.world_rewards: deterministic sigma points and weighted-moment recovery with manifold-aware mean/residual
pressures.observable_consequence: RMS error and filter consistency (NEES) on a bearings-only or reentry tracking problem for the EKF vs the UKF, and with vs without the angular residual function; exact match to the KF on a linear-Gaussian system
pressures.vacuity_condition: a linear-Gaussian system (the UKF reduces to the KF)
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: the true Jacobian where it exists (the EKF's best case, which the world uses as a control)
pressures.cheat_control: on a linear-Gaussian system the UKF must equal the exact Kalman filter to round-off; the EKF must diverge on a strongly nonlinear map where the UKF holds; the angular residual removed must corrupt the heading covariance: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: reference Bayesian filters (Labbe 2014-, with the book)
